questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code serializes or deserializes trip data? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In a 409 fare_above_cap response, how does the estimate field appear in the JSON?
choices: As a JSON number such as 18.5
As a JSON string such as "18.50"
As an object with unscaled value and exponent
The encoder raises TypeError, so the response fails

questions.prompt: A request carries "requested_at": "2024-05-01T10:00:00" (no Z and no offset). What does request_ride return?
choices: 400 saying requested_at must include a UTC offset
500, because the later encoding of a naive datetime fails

questions.prompt: A request has "seats": true and every other field is valid. What happens?
choices: It is accepted with seats equal to 1, since True == 1
It is rejected with 400 because bool is excluded from the integer check
It is accepted and serialized back as true
It raises an unhandled exception, because bool is not an int
